title: Migration 62 — compliance rule conditions
description: Applies migrations 39, 40, 41, 61 then 62, runs 62's VERIFY A-D, then rolls 62 back on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster. A compliance rule could say who it applies to, how much it matters and whether it is in force, but never what makes a batch VIOLATE it -- which is why nothing evaluates rules and a human must link rule to batch by hand for the #157 gate to fire. 62 adds one nullable JSONB column holding the structured predicate from src/lib/complianceRuleCondition.ts. Nullable is the point: every existing rule keeps working, and some regulations genuinely cannot be reduced to a field comparison, so 'has no condition' must stay distinguishable from 'has an empty one'. The CHECK guards SHAPE ONLY -- field names and operator/type agreement are validated by parseRuleCondition in the application, because re-implementing the field registry as a Postgres CHECK would create a second definition of a valid condition that then drifts from the first, which is exactly the divergence migration 61 had just finished closing. Storing a condition still makes nothing enforce: no trigger reads the column and the buyer-pack gate does not consult it.

verify.note: C is the section that matters and it asserts a NEGATIVE that looks like a bug: a condition naming a field that does not exist IS accepted. That is deliberate -- the CHECK is a shape guard, and duplicating the field registry into SQL would recreate the two-definitions defect migration 61 closed. C also proves the shapes that MUST be refused are refused: a bare JSON string (an expression string is precisely what option A rejects), a bare array, and an object carrying none of field/all/any/not. B proves the column is optional and that a rule without a condition is still reported as enforced, so 62 cannot be shown to have disturbed 61.
